title: Tabs, Collapsing Headers and Tooltips
summary: Tools have more settings than fit on one screen. This lesson covers the ways to organise them - collapsing headers, tab bars, and the old Columns API you will meet in existing code - plus tooltips and help markers, so every setting can explain itself.
ideas:
- Build an inspector for one game object with collapsing headers for Transform, Render and Physics, each with tooltips on every field.
- Build a settings window with three tabs and a help marker next to each setting.

cards.q: Which pairs follow the "End only if Begin returned true" rule in this lesson?
cards.a:
BeginTabBar/EndTabBar, BeginTabItem/EndTabItem, and BeginItemTooltip/EndTooltip

BeginTabItem returns true only for the visible tab, so EndTabItem goes inside the if. Only windows and child windows always need their End.

cards.q: How do you select a tab from code?
cards.a:
Pass ImGuiTabItemFlags_SetSelected to its BeginTabItem on that frame

The flag applies on the frame you pass it; the order you submit tabs in does not choose the selected one.

Long unwrapped text makes the tooltip wider than the screen

Pushing a wrap position keeps it readable: PushTextWrapPos(GetFontSize() * 30) wraps at about 30 characters wide.

cards.q: What is the difference between CollapsingHeader and TreeNode?
cards.a:
CollapsingHeader does not push the ID stack and needs no TreePop

It is a full-width, header-style section toggle; TreeNode pushes the ID stack while open and needs TreePop.

cards.q: Which call shows a simple tooltip for the widget just drawn?
cards.a:
ImGui::SetItemTooltip("...")

It shows only when the last item is hovered. An unchecked BeginTooltip would show all the time.

cards.q: You find ImGui::Columns(2) in old code. What should you consider?
cards.a:
Converting it to a two-column table

Columns is legacy and still works; tables do everything it did and more.
